claims.text: In stage 0 the donhang.local:8443 site only served files (tls internal, root, file_server); in stage 1 it also has handle /api/v1/* { reverse_proxy api:8080 }.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-0 and stage-1: Caddyfile donhang.local:8443 block (stage-1 lines 62-76)

claims.text: tls internal makes Caddy issue the site certificate from its own local authority (root + intermediate); in the lab the laptop does not trust that authority, so curl needs -k.
With TLS terminated at Caddy, Caddy decrypts the HTTPS request and forwards it to the upstream api:8080 over plain HTTP (reverse_proxy to an address without https:// uses HTTP).
claims.source_hint: Caddy docs: reverse_proxy upstream addresses / transport; Caddyfile comment line 65

claims.text: DonHang.Api/Dockerfile sets ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://+:8080, so Kestrel listens for plain HTTP on 8080, and the API loads no certificate.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: DonHang.Api/Dockerfile:27; Program.cs (no HTTPS/certificate setup)

claims.text: curl -sk -i --resolve donhang.local:8443:127.0.0.1 https://donhang.local:8443/api/v1/products/1 returns 200 with Server: Kestrel and Via: 1.1 Caddy; without -k, curl rejects the certificate as issued by an untrusted authority.
claims.source_hint: generator check on the running lab (Windows curl: SEC_E_UNTRUSTED_ROOT without -k)

claims.text: From the lab box, curl https://api:8080/... fails with a TLS error (e.g. 'wrong version number'), while curl http://api:8080/... returns the JSON.
claims.source_hint: generator check via ssh into the lab box: curl exit 35, error:0A00010B wrong version number

claims.text: curl's --resolve host:port:address makes that one command connect to the given address for host:port without changing the hosts file; -k skips certificate verification.

The unencrypted proxy-to-upstream part is acceptable only on the same machine or a private network; terminating TLS at the proxy means certificates are managed in one place, however many services are behind it.

Sending a TLS greeting to Kestrel on api:8080 gets a plain HTTP/1.1 400 answer back, which curl cannot read as TLS; both HTTPS and plain requests reach Kestrel as plain HTTP from Caddy (with X-Forwarded-Proto telling the original scheme).
claims.source_hint: reviewer r1 run on the lab; Caddy docs reverse_proxy headers; ASP.NET Core docs: proxy and load balancer
